name: Uma Fischer

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about an ordinary day at the accounting firm.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The water-testing lab sends invoices for sample kits and a separate list of retests it has not charged for, and I reconcile both before preparing its accounts and tax return. I like finding a credit that saves the lab a needless bill; I dislike the late retest list that arrives after the reviewer has booked time for my file. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree and a professional accountancy qualification, and I am an experienced mid-level accountant, not a new starter or a team lead. I use AI now and then to suggest unmatched invoices, but I check the lab order and bank entry myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI does little more, the lab's retest credits still need checking. The draft unmatched list might be quicker, but the order record tells me whether a charge is real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell colleagues to keep the lab order behind each correction. I would tell the lab when a retest has been counted twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am paid below many accountants at my level, and my partner Soren and I have less than a month of expenses saved. Our grown sons live on their own, our rent and heating use most of our pay, and few comparable firms are nearby; that keeps me uneasy even if the technology stalls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing the paid lab accounts and checking approved AI suggestions against source orders. I would stop buying the ready-made lunches at the station twice a week and move the actual saving into cash only if food, rent and travel still fit our wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the bills already on our table. A slow technology year will not make the heating meter run backwards.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the lunch change really save money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if I bring food from home for less than those lunches cost. I would count the actual difference, not the sticker price.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your sons help with rent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown sons have homes of their own. I will ask them to visit, not put their pay in our household budget.

say: I would keep **lab orders** behind each correction so another accountant can trace the charge.
I would flag a **double-counted retest** before filing.
think: Our **low pay** and under-one-month savings make rent and heating fragile.
Few local firms limit any quick **replacement wage**.
do: Keep **paid lab accounts** and verify approved AI suggestions against orders.
Replace **station lunches** with cheaper food and deposit only the actual saving after essentials.
S0.quote: A slow technology year will not make the heating meter run backwards.
fieldNote: Her experience lets her trace **lab retests** while occasional AI stays a source-checked suggestion.
Lunch savings are **new cash** only if cheaper food and essential bills leave a real difference.

steps.text: Keep paid lab returns and check approved invoice suggestions against source orders
Replace station lunches and deposit only actual saving after rent food and travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AI could write the return and match kit invoices faster than I do. Robots may handle lab samples later, but the account and ordering screen would change first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to show us wrong matches and paid-hours plans before changing the rota. I would tell the lab that a missed credit needs a person who can answer for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own mid-level checking hours could be cut when a senior covers more files. With so little saved, even a smaller rota would strain rent, although I can test a useful system and some local work may still be available.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my manager Lina for a paid two-week comparison of AI-matched lab invoices with anonymised signed files, only with written approval. If it passes, I would learn the approved checker on paid time and use it live only after Lina signs the error record; if not, I would keep the authorised paid checks while offered. In the first year, if my hours fall, I would take a posted accounts role only with written pay, hours and start date covering rent, heating and travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about hours, but I can still insist on an honest error count. A missed laboratory credit becomes a real bill before it becomes a chart.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Lina test it?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My manager Lina and I would count false invoice matches and missing retest credits against the signed files. We would not use it live on an unreviewed result.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a posted job has lower pay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the written wage after travel with rent and heating before moving. An advertised title alone does not pay for a winter bill.

I would keep a **named answerer** for missed lab credits.
think: My own **mid-level hours** could shrink with faster checking.
Our tiny reserve makes a smaller rota a **rent and heating risk**.
do: Test **two paid weeks** of anonymised lab invoices against signed files with written approval; otherwise keep paid checks.

feel: I feel **anxious** about possible reduced hours.
S1.quote: A missed laboratory credit becomes a real bill before it becomes a chart.
fieldNote: Her occasional AI use supports a trial, but **signed error evidence** and paid learning govern live deployment.
A job move needs an actual **posted opening** with after-travel pay covering rent and heating.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2028 could match the lab order, decide the retest credit and finish the tax return without my desk. Robots around 2031 would later reach physical sample handling, not delay the accounts change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for written notice of any last paid day and fair severance. I would tell the lab to keep original order records while the firm changes tools.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the firm to end my accounting post when AGI does the matching and checking. Soren's night-security wage cannot cover our rent and heating alone, and our savings would last only weeks; I have been waking at night doing the bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would stop the planned weekend coach trip and move its monthly instalment into cash while paid work continues. I would keep every paid lab file offered; if my post ends in the first year after 2028, I would use the reserve for bills and seek posted sample-intake clerk work at the lab, taking it only with written pay, hours and start date covering rent, heating and travel. Physical intake may last until robots around 2031, so it is a paid bridge, not safety for years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect our main wage to vanish. Knowing the lab order numbers does not make the lab owe me a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you be able to do sample intake?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if the written duties are safe for me and the shifts fit Soren's actual night-security rota. I will not promise I can lift boxes I have not seen.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lab has no vacancy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If no intake role is posted, I would keep the paid firm work while it is offered and use our reserve for bills only after the job ends. I would not write the lab's name in our budget as a salary.

say: I would seek **written last-paid-day notice** and severance.
I would ask the lab to keep **original order records**.
think: I expect my **accounting post** to end in 2028.
Our **weeks of savings** cannot cover rent and heating without my wage.
do: Stop the **coach trip** and deposit its instalment while paid work continues.
Keep **paid lab files** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills.
Take a **posted sample-intake job** only with written safe duties, rent-heating-travel-covering pay, hours, start and Soren-fit rota.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected loss of the main wage.
S2.quote: Knowing the lab order numbers does not make the lab owe me a job.
fieldNote: AGI hits her **2028 desk work** before capable robots reach physical sample handling around 2031.
The bridge requires **safe duties** and rota fit; new cash comes from a cancelled instalment while wages continue.

steps.text: Cancel coach trip and deposit instalment while wages continue
Keep paid lab files while offered; after loss use reserve for bills
Seek posted intake work after 2028 loss only with written bill-covering pay, hours and start
Accept intake duties only if safely manageable and shifts fit Soren’s actual night-security rota

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me a chance to see which lab finance tasks still pay a person before AGI reaches accounts in 2031. Robots around 2034 would later change physical sample handling.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a posted paid purchasing-clerk place if the lab needs someone to question missing kit orders. I would not pay for a course just because a new title sounds tidy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My tax wage may shrink, but I know the lab's order trail and could learn a narrow purchasing task with a supervisor. I am experienced in accounts, not a laboratory scientist or a senior buyer. A purchasing job still uses a screen and could face AGI, so I would treat it as paid bridge work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one disputed kit order monthly only if Lina assigns it with paid supervision and the lab pays the firm for that work. I would keep paid returns; if the lab posts a purchasing-clerk place with a short course, I would enrol only with employer-paid fees and paid study hours, then take the role only with written pay, hours and start date covering rent, heating and travel. In the first year after 2031, if account work ends first, I would use the reserve for bills while seeking that actual paid place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the accounting wage, but five years lets me test paid demand. I would rather see a purchase order than a training poster.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lab will not pay for disputed orders?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would stop the extra task and keep the paid returns still offered. A free favour would not replace my wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Soren cover a longer commute?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if we check his actual rota and the written wage after travel still covers rent and heat. A posted role is not automatically a workable offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A decade puts me at 68 when AGI reaches the account desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 may later change physical lab intake, but I cannot assume my tax post survives until I decide to stop.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a written estimate of any retirement income and tell Soren what it actually says. I would also ask the firm which paid checking hours it expects to keep each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would like to work less eventually, but I do not know whether any income available to me would cover rent and heating. With less than a month saved now, I cannot just turn down paid work because of a birthday.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a written retirement-income estimate and compare it with our actual rent, heating, food and travel bills before changing hours. I would keep paid lab accounts while offered; in the first year after 2036, if they end and the figures do not cover bills, I would use the reserve and take a posted accounts role only with written pay, hours and start date covering those costs after travel. I would reduce my hours only if the firm confirms a paid shorter rota in writing and our combined income covers bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about this month's costs even with ten years to plan. The winter heating bill has a due date whether the future is slow or fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your sons help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown sons have their own homes. I would ask them to help read a statement, not to pay the bill it reveals.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the income estimate is enough?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check the written shorter-hours offer and actual bills with Soren before accepting it. A plausible figure is not an agreed work schedule.

I would check **rent and heating** before changing shifts.
think: I do not know if retirement income covers **rent and heating**.

fieldNote: At 68 she checks **actual income and bills** before reducing hours, with no assumed pension amount.
A shorter paid rota must be **written and affordable**; later work requires a posted wage and existing files count only while offered.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could take the wage that pays our rent before another job is real. Written notice, severance and a posted role with pay that covers heating as well as rent would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how much time a disputed kit order takes when a lab changes its mind. I can trace a disputed kit order, but I cannot make the lab pay the firm for work it does not buy.

headlineQuote: I can trace a disputed kit order, but I cannot make the lab pay the firm for work it does not buy.
portrait: Uma is a **58-year-old experienced mid-level accountant** with a bachelor's degree and professional qualification.
Her **low pay**, under-one-month reserve and few nearby firms make rent and heating persistent worries.
She uses AI **occasionally** but requires paid, signed tests before live use.
She tests **billed purchasing work** and conditions any later hours cut on verified income and a written rota.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case threatens the wage paying rent and heat before another role exists.
whatWouldHelp: She wants **written notice and severance**, plus a posted role covering rent and heating.
